text: U.S. stock indices traded lower on Wednesday as surging Treasury yields and crude oil prices—which climbed above $100 per barrel following renewed geopolitical tensions in the Persian Gulf—weighed on investor sentiment. Market breadth was negative, with the majority of S&P 500 sectors finishing in the red, led by declines in Health Care, Financials, and Materials, while Energy emerged as a notable sector gainer. Volatility also increased, with the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) rising as market participants monitored these inflationary pressures ahead of upcoming producer and consumer price index reports.
